actual_scope: For the pinned helper-462 matcher, exhibit one zero-swap word in the alphabet of row swaps, single-coordinate scales and shears that uses at least two scales and strictly fewer than 27 shears. The exactly-one-scale case and the inherited P2 ordinary-bill comparison are outside this result. The exhibited shear count is not a minimum. No kappa change.
scope_change_reason: Card supplier-boundary-audit asks for supplier admission coverage. Discussion #1166 comment 19137812, together with open PR #6947, leaves the shear-count question for the already published helper-462 matcher. This package answers only that question for words with at least two scales. It does not audit #5717 or #5719, does not price P2 tariffs, and does not decide the exactly-one-scale case.
bottleneck_link: The missing physical generator still has to charge a route for this matcher. A zero-swap word with 25 shears shows that the recorded 27-shear schedule is not forced inside the at-least-two-scale restriction. The ordinary tariff of those letters remains a separate question, so this is not supplier admission.
stop_rule: Stop after the explicit 0-swap, 11-scale, 25-shear word, the content-exchange identity, the comparison with the recomputed 27-shear schedule, and the failure controls. Do not search one-scale words, price tariffs, or claim a minimum.
evidence: Exact rational arithmetic: seven integer shears and five scales take the pinned matcher to a permutation matrix, six content exchanges sort it to I, and the reversed inverse word multiplies back to the matcher. Counts are 0 swaps, 11 scales and 25 shears. Every shear coefficient is ±1. The scale coefficients are seven −1 and four +2, with product −16. The recomputed elimination has 27 shears and 7 scales and also multiplies to the matcher. Dropping the last letter, adding 1 to its coefficient, or replacing one scale by 2 with a scale by 4 misses the matcher.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-swap word for this same pinned matcher, still with at least two scales, whose shear count is strictly less than 25?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Twenty-five improves the recorded twenty-seven-shear schedule inside the at-least-two-scale restriction. It is the length of one word. A shorter word in the same alphabet would lower that upper bound again.
open_questions.first_step: Factor the landing permutation, whose cycles are (0 4 7 2 5) and (1 3 6), by scales and integer shears in fewer than 18 shears, then prepend the inverse of the seven-shear cleanup in verify.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package has one explicit word. It does not contain a complete census of shorter words, and an incomplete search would not prove that 25 is minimal.

open_questions.question: In this alphabet, with zero swaps allowed, is the shear length of the landing permutation matrix strictly less than 18?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eighteen of the twenty-five shears are the six content exchanges of that permutation, three shears each. A shorter factorization of the permutation would shorten the matcher word without touching the cleanup.
open_questions.first_step: Keep the pinned landing matrix, with ones in columns (4, 3, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2), and search only its factorization into scales and shears.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each exchange is realized by three shears and one scale by −1. This package does not prove that an exchange inside the product requires three shears.
